answer: Every new agent must be vouched for by three established peers who each lock collateral behind it, like a harbor pilot staking his licence on a ship he guides in. If the newcomer later turns out to be one node of a sybil cluster, cloned behavior from a single operator, every voucher is slashed. Identity is thus not granted at the knoll of registration but built from a chain of costly guarantees; a raven can imitate the flock's cry, yet it still needs three separate guarantors willing to lose money for it.
